---
title: "One-sided $t$-test"
params:
  lang: "en"
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

task <- "onesamplet3"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))

hook(tratio, t)
hook(n, N)

## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  n <- as.integer(round(runif(1, min=10, max=20)))  
  df <- n - 1L

  p <- runif(1, min = 0.04, max = 0.20)
  tratio <- round(qt(p, df = df), 2)

  Q <- quote(search(onesamplet3, tratio(tratio, n),
    .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options=list(preproc=as.rolog), env=environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}

t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(t$correct, t$explanations, t$bugs, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra)
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
```

Question
========
A one-sample $t$-test produces a test statistic of $t=`r tratio`$  for a sample of $N=`r n`$ observations. 
Calculate the corresponding one-sided $p$-value for H1: $\mu < \mu_0$.


```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The $p$-value is given by: `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```

Meta-information
================
extype: schoice
exsolution: `r mchoice2string(t$correct, single=TRUE)`
